post.description: Story 6-1a: a session answer also sets the httpOnly refresh cookie (`wms_refresh`, path /api/v1/tenants/session). Attempts are counted per (email, client IP) BEFORE the password check: 5 consecutive failures lock that pair for 15 minutes (423 for any password, real or unknown email alike); 300 attempts a minute per client IP answer 429. Story 6-1b: a user with two-factor sign-in set up gets `TotpChallengeResponse`; an owner who has not set it up yet gets `EnrollChallengeResponse` — both create no session and set no cookie, and are completed at `POST /tenants/sign-in/second-factor`. Clients tell the arms apart by the presence of `challenge`. A web client that can complete the second step sends `X-WMS-Second-Factor: 1`; without it, a sign-in that needs the second step answers 409 `client-outdated` and writes nothing.

parameters.name: X-WMS-Second-Factor
parameters.description: Story 6-1b — `1` from a client that can complete the second step

400.description: Invalid body

401.description: Unknown email, wrong password, or a deactivated account (unauthenticated — one answer for all three)

403.description: Invitation not yet accepted (invite-pending), a client-portal user whose client is suspended (client-suspended, story 21-7) or has departed (client-departed, story 1-2a), or — story 6-1b — an owner reset this user’s two-factor sign-in and the enrolment code has expired (enrolment-code-expired: ask for another reset; nothing counted)

409.description: Story 6-1b — the second step is needed and the client did not send `X-WMS-Second-Factor: 1` (client-outdated: "Reload this page to sign in"); nothing was written

423.description: Too many failed attempts for this email from this address — or, story 6-1c, on this browser’s device cookie (sign-in-locked; `retryAfterSeconds`)

429.description: Too many attempts from this address, or (story 6-1c) too many untrusted attempts for this account or from this address this hour (rate-limited; `retryAfterSeconds`)

post.summary: Verifies the password; opens a server-side session — or, story 6-1b, asks for the second factor first

post.description: Not keyed: it issues a credential. A `totp` challenge takes a 6-digit code (steps t−1…t+1, each usable once) or a backup code; an `enroll` challenge takes a code from the newly set-up app (and, after an owner’s reset, the one-time `enrolmentCode`), then answers the ten backup codes once. Every attempt is counted BEFORE the code is checked: 5 consecutive wrong codes lock two-factor sign-in for 15 minutes; the third lock without a success lasts until an owner unlocks it. Sets the refresh cookie like sign-in.

400.description: Invalid body

401.description: Wrong code (second-factor-invalid; `attemptsLeft`), or the challenge is unknown, expired, used, out of attempts, or the account changed (challenge-ended — sign in again)

423.description: Too many wrong codes (second-factor-locked; `retryAfterSeconds`, null until an owner unlocks)

429.description: Too many attempts from this address (rate-limited; `retryAfterSeconds`)

503.description: The stored secret cannot be opened with the configured key (second-factor-unavailable); nothing was counted

post.summary: Story 6-1b — completes a sign-in with the second factor and opens the session

post.description: Unauthenticated and unkeyed. Answers 202 with ONE body for every email: a link (single use, 60 minutes) is mailed only to an active user — and for a client-portal user, only while their client is active. An unknown, invited or deactivated email queues nothing. A user holds at most 5 live links (a sixth request spends the oldest); at most 5 links are mailed per user per rolling hour (past that, the same 202 and nothing queued). 20 requests an hour per client address answer 429.

400.description: Invalid body

429.description: Too many reset requests from this address this hour (rate-limited; `retryAfterSeconds`)

post.summary: Story 6-1c — asks for a password-reset link by email

post.description: The reset page calls it on load (opening the link spends nothing). One 400 `reset-link-invalid` for a malformed, unknown, wrong, expired or spent token, a user who is not active and a client-portal user whose client is not active.

400.description: Invalid body, or the link is not valid (reset-link-invalid)

429.description: Too many reset attempts from this address (rate-limited; `retryAfterSeconds`)

post.summary: Story 6-1c — validates a reset link; changes nothing

post.description: Unkeyed; signs no one in and issues no session (the next sign-in runs the lockout and, for an enrolled user, the second step unchanged). An enrolled user must send `code` (TOTP or backup code); wrong codes are counted on the link (the 5th spends it), never on the user, and a live two-factor lock answers 423. On success every session of the user ends (`password-reset`), every link is spent, open sign-in steps end, every lockout for the email clears, and a password-changed notice is mailed. Sets the `wms_device` cookie (the browser that completed the reset is trusted at its next sign-in). A retry after success answers 400 `reset-link-invalid`.

400.description: Invalid body (the password is 8–200 characters), or the link is not valid (reset-link-invalid)

422.description: The account uses two-factor sign-in and no code was sent, or its factor changed since the check (second-factor-needed — nothing counted); or the code is wrong (second-factor-invalid; `attemptsLeft`)

423.description: Two-factor sign-in is locked for this account (second-factor-locked; `retryAfterSeconds`, null until an owner unlocks)

429.description: Too many reset attempts from this address, or too many codes tried on reset links for this account today (rate-limited; `retryAfterSeconds`)

503.description: The stored second-factor secret cannot be opened with the configured key (second-factor-unavailable); nothing was counted

post.summary: Story 6-1c — sets a new password from a reset link

post.description: Cookie-only (`wms_refresh`); requires an allow-listed Origin and `X-WMS-Session: 1`. Refresh never extends the idle window. A rotated token presented within 30 s is a tab race (a new access token, no new cookie); after that it is reuse and the session is revoked.

401.description: No session to refresh (unauthenticated), or the session is over (session-ended with `reason`: signed-out | deactivated | role-changed | client-suspended | client-departed | refresh-reuse | idle | absolute)

403.description: Origin not allow-listed or the X-WMS-Session header missing (role-denied)

post.summary: Story 6-1a — rotates the refresh cookie and issues a new access token

post.description: Names the session by the refresh cookie, else by the bearer token (an expired access token still works). Idempotent. Requires an allow-listed Origin and `X-WMS-Session: 1`.

204.description: Signed out (or there was nothing to sign out)

403.description: Origin not allow-listed or the X-WMS-Session header missing (role-denied)

post.description: labels.execute (owner, ops manager, operator). Send `binIds` (1–1000 distinct bins of this warehouse) or `zoneId` (the zone's non-retired, non-system bins; more than 1000 is refused). Labels come out sorted by bin code (numeric collation, ties by code then id). Each label carries the code in large text, a Code 128 (start B) of exactly the code, `<ZONE> - <WAREHOUSE>`, and a small line with the storage class when not ambient and the dedicated client's code. `layout=label` prints one label per page / per ^XA…^XZ at `size` 4x2 (default) or 2x1 in; `layout=a4` (PDF only) prints 24 per A4 sheet (3 × 8 cells of 70 × 36 mm). The listing refusals carry `binCodes` (the first 50 offenders). The `Content-Disposition` filename (`bin-labels-<WH>-<YYYYMMDD>.<ext>`, the IST date) is not readable cross-origin — a client builds the same name itself.

post.summary: dispatch.execute — closes a packed order: the TERMINAL transition of the order state machine. One zero-quantity dispatch.dispatched ledger event per order line records the shipment (the units left stock at pick, so nothing moves), the order flips ready_to_dispatch → dispatched, and every committed reservation the order still owns is retired to released — the transition that finally restores the reserved counter and corrects ATP. The flip, the events, the retirements, the outbox event, the audit row and the idempotency key all commit in ONE transaction; the Valkey counter mirror follows the commit. Carrier and tracking number are optional free text. There is no un-dispatch: the arm is terminal.

201.description: Pick recorded: the pick snapshot with suggestion-vs-actual bin/batch (the idempotency snapshot — a replay re-serves it, nothing re-draws). On a short pick it also carries the shortfall, the reason, whether the hold was released and re-granted, and the slices the remainder was re-planned onto (empty on the partial-order path)

400.description: Missing or malformed Idempotency-Key, an invalid body, a quantity ABOVE the line’s planned quantity, a short pick with no reasonCode or one outside the fixed set (the 400 names the whole set), a blocked bin (bin-blocked — unless the pick was made before the block, story 3-3b, and the block is neither backfilled nor a contamination or temperature-excursion block; a zero-unit `skipped-blocked-bin` short of the planned stop is admitted), a `skipped-blocked-bin` reason with qty above 0 or at another bin than the stop’s (validation-failed), a retired bin (bin-retired), a system bin, the wrong item scanned (wrong-item naming the expected SKU), or a serial-arm violation (validation-failed)

401.description: Missing/invalid device token, or a bare device credential without badge-in (unauthenticated)

403.description: Session belongs to another tenant (permission-denied), unknown or revoked device (device-revoked), or the operator lacks picks.execute (role-denied)

404.description: Warehouse, picklist line, order, SKU or bin does not exist in this tenant (not-found)

409.description: AD-14 case 3 — the bin’s state_epoch moved and it no longer covers the draw (pick-bin-short, naming the bin and its live on-hand; RE-PLANNABLE, the client keeps the op). AD-14 case 4 — a premise moved terminally: the hold is expired/terminal, or the line, picklist, wave or order was cancelled or already picked (pick-unresolvable; TERMINAL, the client quarantines with session attribution). Also: the wave is not yet released / the picklist is not yet ready (conflict, retryable), a concurrent idempotent request (conflict), or a serial that does not live in the scanned bin (serial-elsewhere); story 3-7a — the scanned bin holds on-hand of a batch of this SKU on an OPEN LIVE recall: an unscanned draw cannot tell the recalled units from good ones, so move them out first (recalled-lot-in-bin, members binCode, batchCodes, recallCodes; TERMINAL for the queued op — it lands in review); story 3-3b — a `skipped-blocked-bin` Skip of a stop whose bin is no longer blocked (bin-not-blocked, member binCode — the stop is still planned; pick it normally). None of these persist anything and none consume the idempotency key

422.description: Idempotency key reused with a different payload (idempotency-key-reuse), or the bin drained before this (queued) pick replayed with NO bin epoch to prove it moved (insufficient-on-hand, naming the bin’s live on-hand — nothing persists; this is the pre-4.3b behaviour a device that has not refreshed still gets)

post.summary: pick.record — records one scan-verified pick exactly once (badge-in session required): the pick.picked ledger draw empties the scanned bin and the order line’s reservation settles held → committed in the SAME transaction; the line flips to picked. Story 4.3b: the optional binStateEpoch is compared under the bin’s row lock before any write and classifies a conflict by the AD-14 taxonomy — apply/settle answer 201, pick-bin-short is re-plannable, pick-unresolvable is terminal. Story 4.4: a qty BELOW the line’s plan is a short pick and needs a reasonCode — the draw, the whole hold’s release, the re-grant of the remainder, the line’s flip to short and the re-planned slice all commit together; a zero-unit short pick reports an empty bin and writes no ledger event and no picks row

post.summary: pack.execute — the DEVICE bench route (badge-in session required): the same packOrder command the tenant route delegates to, with the order id in the body. The scan is compared against what the order actually had PICKED; a discrepancy is refused (422 pack-mismatch) naming the SKU and both quantities before anything is written. On a match, the accepted → ready_to_dispatch flip, the zero-quantity pack.packed events, the outbox, the audit and the idempotency key commit in ONE transaction and the packing slip is returned. Parcel weight is optional; dimensions are NOT part of the device payload (the web surface keeps that arm)

post.description: labels.execute (owner, ops manager, operator). Send `lpnIds` (1–1000 distinct LPNs of this receipt — a reprint), or `grnLineId` (the line's LPNs that are not voided), or neither (every LPN of the receipt that is not voided; more than 1000 is refused — print in parts). Labels come out in code order. Each carries the code in large text, a Code 128 (start B) of exactly the code, `<SKU> x <qty> <uom>`, and `<GRN> | B <batch> EXP <date> | CLIENT <code>` (the batch part when batched, the expiry when set, the client when not the tenant's own). A placed LPN still prints. `layout=label` prints one label per page / per ^XA…^XZ at `size` 4x2 (default) or 2x1 in; `layout=a4` (PDF only) prints 24 per A4 sheet. The listing refusals carry `lpnCodes` (the first 50 offenders). The `Content-Disposition` filename (`lpn-labels-<GRN>-<YYYYMMDD>.<ext>`, the IST date) is not readable cross-origin — a client builds the same name itself.

get.description: READ-ONLY reconstruction from `ledger_events` alone — never from projections, never from the temperature_excursions rows. The join chain: the dispatch events whose reference doc names the order → the pick events with the same orderId → those picks’ batch/serial scopes → each scope’s complete chain (other orders’ picks included — the batch’s history is the batch’s history). STORAGE-CLASS CAVEAT: every chain event is annotated with the bins’ CURRENT storage class. The report never fabricates historical classes it cannot prove; the annotation is honest because the class-edit guards refuse a change that would strand stock (temperature classes may only have moved colder for bins that held stock). Excursion correlation is dwell-window based, from the ledger alone: an excursion.recorded event attaches to a scope when its skuId matches the line, its reference doc’s binId is a bin on that scope’s chain, and its business time falls inside that bin’s dwell window — [first arrival, last departure], open-ended when the scope was still there at pick time. An excursion recorded before arrival or after departure does not appear.

post.description: Creates the invoice when the dispatch event has not yet (or never — pre-8-1 dispatches have no backfill) produced one; otherwise recomputes it. An invoice issues (and takes the next number of its supplier GSTIN's FY series, e.g. 29/2627/000001, once) when every dispatched line is priced, the place of supply resolves and a supplier GSTIN exists (warehouse, else tenant); otherwise it stays 'awaiting-data' with its gaps listed in the document. An issued invoice is FROZEN: a plain regenerate returns it unchanged (no recompute, whatever the catalog now says), and rates sent to it are refused (invoice-frozen). Content-identical regeneration of an awaiting invoice leaves the revision unchanged. Overrides never write order_lines.rate_paise. A concurrent generation (the event delivery racing this call) settles to one invoice — on losing the insert this call retries once over the winner's row: if the winner parked awaiting-data the retry's rates apply; if the winner already issued, the retry hits the freeze and answers 409 invoice-frozen.

Only issued invoices count (never awaiting-data or voided). Rows group by (HSN, UQC, GST rate); every amount is the exact paise sum of the frozen invoice lines — nothing is rounded per row and the invoice round-off is never spread. A line whose HSN is blank or malformed (not 4, 6 or 8 digits) is an hsnIssue row: inside the totals, listed in issueLines with the SKU's current catalog HSN as a hint, and left out of the Table 12 CSV by the client. A row whose GST rate is not on the GST rate master (0, 0.1, 0.25, 1, 1.5, 3, 5, 6, 7.5, 12, 18, 28, 40 %) is a rateIssue row: inside the totals and left out of the Table 12 CSV by the client. The totals equal the included invoices' subtotal and GST to the paisa. A well-formed GSTIN with nothing issued in the period is an empty summary.

info.title: WMS API
info.description: Warehouse Management System backend — modular monolith. This document is the contract: web and mobile clients generate typed clients from it (AD-8).

detail.example: Echo body must be a JSON object

gstin.description: The tenant GSTIN, optional (story 8-1) — the invoicing default the warehouse GSTIN overrides. The settings-edit route is deferred (stamped at registration only).
The tenant GSTIN (8-1); null when none registered.

clientId.description: Story 21-7 — the client brand a client-portal user belongs to (role `client`); null for the tenant’s own staff

lockedUntil.description: Story 6-1a — sign-in is locked for this email (5 failed attempts from one address) until this instant; on the user list only, null or absent when not locked

secondFactorEnabled.description: Story 6-1b — the user has two-factor sign-in set up; on the user list only (absent on stored invite / role-change snapshots)

secondFactorResetPending.description: Story 6-1b — an owner reset this user’s two-factor sign-in and they have not set it up again (an enrolment code is outstanding); on the user list only

accessToken.description: HS256 session token (15 min), claims: sub + tenant_id (+ client_id for a client-portal user, story 21-7)

refreshExpiresInSeconds.description: Story 6-1a — seconds until the session can no longer be refreshed (its absolute end). The refresh token itself rides an httpOnly cookie; the client stores this to tell a refreshable session from an ended one.

client.description: Story 21-7 — the client brand of a client-portal user (the portal shell prints its name); null for the tenant’s own staff

challengeToken.description: The one-time token for `POST /tenants/sign-in/second-factor` (no session exists yet)
The one-time token for `POST /tenants/sign-in/second-factor` (no session exists yet)

binStateEpoch.description: Story 4.3b (AD-14): the scanned bin’s state_epoch as the device read it from the sealed snapshot at task start. Opaque and compared only for equality — never interpreted. Omit it (or send null) and the replay behaves exactly as it did before this story: a device whose cache predates the field is never refused for the absence of it.

reasonCode.description: Story 4.4: why this stop came up short. REQUIRED whenever qty is below the line’s planned quantity (including 0), refused outside the fixed set with a 400 naming the whole set, and ignored when qty equals the plan (that is an ordinary full pick). It is part of the idempotency payload hash — the reason is intent, not an observation. Story 3-3b: `skipped-blocked-bin` skips a planned stop whose bin is now blocked — only with qty 0 at the stop's own bin (else 400 validation-failed) and only while the bin is blocked (else 409 bin-not-blocked); it re-plans the stop onto other bins and needs no bin scan.

id.description: The picks row id — NULL on a zero-unit short pick (story 4.4), which writes no picks row at all: nothing moved, so there is no ledger event and no settlement record. Every other pick, short or whole, has one.

binId.description: The bin the units were actually drawn from

reasonCode.description: Why the stop came up short (story 4.4); null on a whole-quantity pick

conflictClass.description: Story 4.3b (AD-14): the taxonomy arm this pick settled under — none (no epoch sent, or the bin’s epoch still matched), applied (the epoch had moved and the draw stood on its own), settled (the moved-on bin still covered the draw and this pick settled the order line’s hold). The taxonomy’s two refusal arms write nothing, so they never appear here.

What the operator scanned into the parcel. May be empty only when the order picked nothing at all (every stop reported an empty bin).

cartons.description: Story 4-5a — optional: the cartons the parcel was packed into, in order (carton 1 first). Per SKU the cartons must add up to `scanned` exactly, a catch-weight case sits in exactly one carton, and the top-level weightGrams and dimensionsMm must then be absent (weigh each carton). Omitted, the pack is one carton holding the whole scan. The device never measures boxes, so a carton carries no dimensionsMm.

awb.description: The AWB / LR number as stored (normalised)
The AWB / LR number, normalised (trimmed, upper-cased, spaces and hyphens stripped): 4–50 letters, digits or "/"

courierName.description: The courier by name (1–100 characters) — or name a transporter partner; exactly one

transporterId.description: A transporter partner as the courier — or type its name; exactly one

replace.description: Replace the order’s live client label or AWB (before the handover)

reason.description: Why the shipment is voided, 1–200 characters

scannedCode.description: The scanned (or typed) AWB — compared normalised

occurredAt.description: The handheld’s scan instant (required on the device; refused-as-ignored on the web — null there)

verified.description: True when this request verified the label; false when it already was (a no-op that stores the key)

url.description: A short-lived presigned URL; null when unsigned

parcelTagCode.description: The parcel tag’s code (`O` + the order id’s last 16 hex digits)

reason.description: Why, 1–200 characters

transporterId.description: A transporter partner — or name it; exactly one

awb.description: The AWB scanned on the parcel (required with no verified client label)

weightGrams.description: Weight in grams, 1–1,000,000 (default: the live pack’s gross when ≤ 1,000,000 g, else the last pack measurement)

cartonCodes.description: Story 4-5a (A21) — the carton labels scanned onto the pickup (≤ 200; trimmed and upper-cased; an empty list is absent; unique by carton). A code that is not one of this order’s live cartons refuses the parcel (carton-not-current)

clientId.description: One handover carries one client’s parcels

occurredAt.description: The pickup time: on the web within the last 7 days (default now); required on the handheld

note.description: Up to 500 characters

photoRefs.description: The handheld’s signed-sheet photo refs (≤ 10; refused on the web)

code.description: HO-NNNN

complianceException.description: Story 4-6a (A14) — a handheld parcel that left without the brand's documents (a stale snapshot): handed over and flagged, never refused. Absent otherwise

orderStatus.description: The order’s status as read under its lock (e.g. cancelled vs accepted for order-not-ready); absent when the order was not found

handover.description: Null when every parcel of a handheld handover was refused (the review row holds them)

refused.description: Handheld only: the parcels refused into one review row (Discard only)

rejectedOpId.description: The review row’s op id (derived from the key)

cartonCount.description: The live pack’s cartons (1 for an order packed before cartons were recorded)

scanned.description: Cartons scanned onto this pickup (recorded on the carton)

legacy.description: Packed before cartons were recorded: "1 carton (packed before cartons were recorded)"

codCartonScanned.description: A44 — a COD order whose cartons were scanned: false when carton 1 (the COD label) was not; null when not judged

staleCartonLabels.description: A37 — the handheld scanned a superseded pack’s label (accepted, not recorded): reprint the labels

cartons.description: Story 4-5a (A21, A34, A37, A44) — the order’s cartons at this handover

taxDocument.description: Story 4-6a (A19) — the brand’s document the parcel LEFT under (the stamped version); null when none was recorded

ewayBillNumber.description: Story 4-6a — the stamped version’s e-way bill number

ewayValidUntil.description: Story 4-6a — the stamped version’s e-way validity (YYYY-MM-DD)

complianceException.description: Story 4-6a (A14) — a handheld parcel that left without its documents

lateRecord.description: Story 4-6a (A39) — the live version recorded after the dispatch (it clears an exception)

code.description: HO-NNNN

pickupPersonPhone.description: Unmasked for a dispatch.execute holder; masked otherwise

clientSnapshot.description: The client as frozen at the handover (ClientPartySnapshotV1)

warehouseSnapshot.description: The warehouse as frozen at the handover

courierSnapshot.description: The transporter as frozen (TransporterSnapshotV1), when one was named

packSeq.description: Story 4-5a (A21) — the live pack’s number; absent for an order packed before cartons were recorded (one carton, pack 1)

cartonCount.description: Story 4-5a (A21) — the live pack’s carton count; absent as packSeq

defaultWeightGrams.description: Story 4-5a (A33) — the handover’s weight default: the live pack’s gross when ≤ 1,000,000 g (null above it), else the last pack measurement

consignment.description: Story 4-6a (A16) — the brand's documents gate today; a blocking candidate cannot be ticked

reason.description: Why the record is withdrawn (1–200)

consignor.description: The brand as frozen when recorded

destinationStateCode.description: The ship-to state code; null when unknown

thresholdPaise.description: The threshold in force on the document date (null: no bill required)

dispatchedAt.description: Set on the version the goods left under (immutable)

declaredBelowRatedValue.description: A40 — the declared value is below the order's own rated value (a warning)

type.description: The brand's tax invoice, delivery challan or bill of supply

date.description: The document date (YYYY-MM-DD, IST) — no later than today and no earlier than 30 days before the order's creation day

number.description: The brand's e-way bill number (12 digits) — recorded, never generated

date.description: The e-way bill date (YYYY-MM-DD, IST): not before the document, not after today

validUntil.description: Its last valid day (YYYY-MM-DD) — required: the goods move, so Part B is filled (A34)

reason.description: Why no e-way bill is needed above the threshold (an office role on the staff surface — A46)

note.description: Required for "other" (1–200)

brandDocument.description: Required — the brand's tax document the goods travel under

consignorGstin.description: The brand registration the document names (defaults to the client's GSTIN)

declaredValuePaise.description: Required — the consignment value on the brand's document, including tax, in paise (0–10^12); the e-way threshold is judged from it

ewayExemption.description: Instead of an e-way bill — never both

reason.description: Why it is amended (1–200) — required once the order is dispatched

valueFloorPaise.description: max(the order's rated value, its COD amount) — null when it carries neither

history.description: Superseded and withdrawn versions, newest first

dispatchedRecordId.description: The version the goods left under

duplicates.description: Other live records of the client with the same document (a warning)

consignorStateMismatch.description: The consignor's state differs from the warehouse GSTIN's (a warning; false when the warehouse's state is unknown)

ewayUsedByOtherClient.description: The same e-way number is live under another client (staff only)

scans.description: 4-4a's shipping documents of kinds invoice, challan and eway-bill

complianceException.description: A device handover that left without the documents

needed.description: Packed orders first; at most 5,000 scanned

poLineId.description: The PO line received against — null on a blind receipt's lines

asnLineId.description: Story 21-6 — the ASN line received against (only beside asnId). A line with no line reference, or whose SKU differs from the referenced line's, settles unmatched: applied in full, crediting no line

batchCode.description: Catalog batch code (required for batch-tracked SKUs, forbidden otherwise)

mfgDate.description: Optional batch mfg date (ISO-8601 UTC, Z-suffixed). Story 2-4b — a date-only mfg is sent as its date at midnight UTC (`YYYY-MM-DDT00:00:00Z`); ONLY that shape feeds the shelf-life derivation (a batch-tracked line with no typed expiry gets expiry = the mfg's IST date + the SKU's shelfLifeDays). Any other instant is stored as before and derives nothing (a pre-2-4b handheld's misread date arrives as an IST-midnight instant)

expiryDate.description: Story 1-2b — the batch's expiry date as the label states it: an IST calendar date YYYY-MM-DD (a malformed one is a 400). Omit when there is none. Every rule about it is a per-line refusal: on an untracked SKU (`expiry-on-untracked`), before the line's mfg date (`expiry-before-mfg`), unlike the batch's existing expiry or another line's for the same batch (`batch-expiry-mismatch`), missing when the client requires it (`expiry-required`), or fewer days away than the client's minimum (`shelf-life-short`, its own review row)

qty.description: The GOOD units received (story 2-4a — damaged units go in damagedQty, never here; 0 on an all-damaged line, but every line needs qty + damagedQty > 0). A quantity in the SKU's base UoM, at the decimal precision that unit declares (each = 0 places, kg = 3). A value finer than its unit allows is refused, naming the unit and its precision — never silently rounded.

damagedQty.description: Story 2-4a — units that arrived DAMAGED, booked into the warehouse's system DAMAGED bin (not sellable) and never crediting the PO or ASN line. Needs damageReasonCode when > 0. Refused (400) on a serial-tracked or catch-weight SKU. Omit (or 0) when none

damageReasonCode.description: Story 2-4a — why the damaged units are damaged; given exactly when damagedQty > 0

shortQty.description: Story 2-4a — units the supplier's invoice or challan listed that never arrived, typed at the dock. Recorded on the line only — no stock and no effect on the PO or ASN. Needs shortReasonCode when > 0. Omit (or 0) when none

shortReasonCode.description: Story 2-4a — why the units are short; given exactly when shortQty > 0

weightsGrams.description: Catch weight (story 10.3): one captured weight in whole GRAMS per physical unit on this line — required for a catch-weight-tracked SKU, refused for every other SKU, and exactly qty entries long. It is a per-unit actual weight, never a quantity and never the parcel weight pack records.

photoRefs.description: Story 2-5a — the line's damage photos, by the ULID the handheld minted at capture (each photo's own upload op's Idempotency-Key), in capture order. At most 10 per line and 50 per receipt, unique across the receipt. A photo uploaded first is attached by this receipt; one that arrives later fills the placeholder this receipt leaves. A ref that is unknown to this device, or already bound, is skipped — never a refusal. Omit when the line has none (an empty array means the same)

serials.description: Story 2-6a — the line's serial numbers (one per GOOD unit, in capture order), required on a serial-tracked SKU's line and refused on any other: `qty` must equal the count. Each is trimmed, then must be 1–64 printable ASCII characters with no whitespace; case-sensitive; none may repeat for the same SKU across the receipt; ≤ 500 per line (with unreadableSerialQty) and ≤ 1,000 per receipt — each a 400. On an `imei` SKU each must be a 15-digit, Luhn-valid IMEI. A serial already in stock, in transit, on a pending over-receipt, dispatched on an order, blocked, or (imei) badly formed is refused PER SERIAL into `rejectedLines` (`serialsOnly`) and the rest of the line books. Omit (or send an empty array) when the line has none

unreadableSerialQty.description: Story 2-6a — units of a serial-tracked line whose serial could not be read: RECORDED on the line, never booked or credited (set them aside and report). Needs at least one serial on the line; counts toward the 500-per-line cap. Omit (or 0) when none

warehouseId.description: Warehouse the receipt lands in

poId.description: The purchase order received against — exactly one of poId, asnId and blindReasonCode

asnId.description: Story 21-6 — the advance shipment notice received against — exactly one of poId, asnId and blindReasonCode

blindReasonCode.description: The blind-receive reason code (required when neither poId nor asnId is given, forbidden otherwise)

clientId.description: Story 1-1 — the client a BLIND receipt is for (named only beside blindReasonCode; a PO or ASN receipt takes its document's client, and naming one there is a 400). Absent (an older build): the client is derived from the first line's SKU. A line whose SKU belongs to another client is refused per line (`sku-client-mismatch` in rejectedLines) and the rest settles. An unknown client is a 404

gateInId.description: Story 2-3a — the gate-in (the vehicle visit) this receipt came off. NEVER refused (decision 5): an unknown id, a non-uuid or another warehouse's gate-in books the receipt UNLINKED and the answer says why in `gateInLink`; a gated-out gate-in links. Absent: the receipt books exactly as before

occurredAt.description: Device time of the receipt (ISO-8601 UTC, Z-suffixed)

lines.description: The physically received lines

reason.description: `unknown`: no such gate-in (or not a uuid); `other-warehouse`: it is another warehouse's

mfgDate.description: The mfg date it was derived from (YYYY-MM-DD, IST) — the batch's stored mfg, else the first line's

shelfLifeDays.description: The SKU's shelf life used, in days from manufacture

poLineId.description: The PO line credited — null on a blind, ASN or unmatched line. Story 21-9: on a late receipt (a closed PO) the line the excess pends against, null when it matched none

asnLineId.description: Story 21-6 — the ASN line credited; present only when one was. Story 21-9: on a late receipt (a cancelled or closed ASN) the line the excess pends against, when it matched one

qty.description: The good units that arrived (story 2-4a — damaged units are damagedQty; 0 on an all-damaged line)

appliedQty.description: The within-open portion applied immediately — 0 on every line of a late receipt (story 21-9)

excessQty.description: The excess pended for approval — the whole quantity on a late receipt against a closed or cancelled document (story 21-9)

toleranceQty.description: Story 1-2b — the part of appliedQty past the open quantity that booked at once within the client's receiving tolerance (no over-receipt). Present only when > 0

damagedQty.description: Story 2-4a — the units that arrived damaged, booked into the system DAMAGED bin (not sellable). Present only when > 0

damageReasonCode.description: Story 2-4a — why; present only beside damagedQty

shortQty.description: Story 2-4a — the units short against the supplier's document (recorded only). Present only when > 0

shortReasonCode.description: Story 2-4a — why; present only beside shortQty

handlingUnitIds.description: Catch weight (story 10.3): the handling units this line produced, in the order their weights were supplied — present only on a catch-weight line. These ids are what a unit label carries and what the pack bench scans back.

serials.description: Story 2-6a — the serial numbers this line BOOKED now (one `grn.received` each), in capture order; present only on a serial line that booked some

pendingSerials.description: Story 2-6a — the serial numbers set aside on this line's over-receipt (they book, in order, when it is approved); present only when some pend

unreadableSerialQty.description: Story 2-6a — units recorded without a readable serial (not booked); present only when > 0

qcSkipped.description: Story 2-6a — present on a serial line of a QC-on-receipt client's receipt: it booked UNHELD (QC on receipt does not hold serial-tracked lines)

derivedExpiry.description: Story 2-4b — present only when this receipt DERIVED the line's batch expiry: no line typed one and the batch had none, so it is the mfg's IST date + the SKU's shelf life

replacedDerivedExpiry.description: Story 2-4b — present only when a typed expiry on this receipt REPLACED the batch's earlier derived one: that derived date (YYYY-MM-DD, IST)

need.description: What the goods need: drug-20b (G/H/H1), drug-21b (C/C1), drug-20g (X), ndps, or fssai (food)

holder.description: `client` — the brand holds no valid licence for this site (or for none); `site` — the site holds no valid licence

siteCode.description: The receipt's site code — the site a site licence is missing at, or a client licence is missing for

serial.description: The refused serial number, as sent (trimmed)

binCode.description: The bin code it is in (in stock), or the in-transit bin

skuCode.description: An imei SKU: the OTHER SKU this IMEI is held under

poLineId.description: The PO line named — null on an ASN line rejection

asnLineId.description: Story 21-6 — the ASN line named; present only on an ASN line rejection

qty.description: The line's good units, as sent (story 2-4a — 0 on an all-damaged line)

damagedQty.description: Story 2-4a — the refused line's damaged units, as sent (not booked — the line went to review whole). Present only when > 0

shortQty.description: Story 2-4a — the refused line's short units, as sent. Present only when > 0

code.description: Machine reason. Only an OPEN document rejects a line. `po-line-not-open` is defensive since story 21-9 (an open PO has no cancelled or carried line) and stays in the enum for older clients. Story 1-1: `sku-client-mismatch` — a BLIND receipt's line whose SKU belongs to another client than the receipt's; it goes to the review queue (Discard only). Story 1-2a: `client-departed` — a line of ANY receipt whose SKU's client has departed; also to review (Discard only — re-receive after an owner reactivates the client). Story 1-2b — the expiry rules, each per line: `expiry-on-untracked`, `expiry-before-mfg`, `batch-expiry-mismatch`, `expiry-required` (review, Discard only) and `shelf-life-short` (its own review row — Accept anyway with a note, or Discard). Story 1-6d: `licence-not-covered` — licence enforcement is on and no valid client and site licence covers the line's drug or food goods on the receipt's IST date; its own review row (`grn.licence-refused` — an owner may accept it anyway with a note, or discard it). Story 2-6a — serial capture, all to `grn.lines-refused` (Discard only): the WHOLE line is refused `serials-required` (a serial-tracked SKU sent without serials — an older build or queued op) or `serials-on-untracked` (serials on a SKU that is not serial-tracked); PER SERIAL (`serialsOnly`, the rest books — or the whole line when every serial is refused): `serial-format-invalid` (not a valid IMEI on an imei SKU), `serial-in-stock` (on hand in any bin of any warehouse, or — imei — under another imei SKU), `serial-in-transit` (on a transfer), `serial-pending-approval` (on another receipt's open over-receipt), `serial-dispatched-use-returns` (it left on an order — receive it as a return) and `serial-blocked`

reason.description: Human-readable reason naming the line state

index.description: Story 1-2b — the line's index in the request (present on an expiry refusal and — 1-6d — a licence refusal only)

batchCode.description: Story 1-2b — the line's batch code (present on an expiry refusal only)

expiryDate.description: Story 1-2b — the expiry date the rule judged (YYYY-MM-DD, IST): the line's own, or for `expiry-required` / `shelf-life-short` the effective one (the line's, else its batch's); null when none. Present on an expiry refusal only

minShelfLifeDays.description: Story 1-2b — `shelf-life-short` only: the client's minimum remaining shelf life in days (0 when the client sets none — the batch had expired)

missing.description: Story 1-6d — `licence-not-covered` only: each need no valid licence covers on the receipt's IST date, and which holder lacks it (the entry also carries `index`)

serials.description: Story 2-6a — the refused serial numbers (a serial refusal), or the refused line's serials (a `serials-*` line refusal)

serialsOnly.description: Story 2-6a — ONLY these serials of line `index` were refused; the rest of the line booked (qty = the refused count)

serialDetails.description: Story 2-6a — per refused serial: where it is, or the other IMEI SKU holding it

unreadableSerialQty.description: Story 2-6a — a whole-line refusal's unreadable units (not booked); present only when > 0

derivedExpiry.description: Story 2-4b — present only on an expiry refusal whose judged expiry the receipt DERIVED from mfg + shelf life (`shelf-life-short`, or a `batch-expiry-mismatch` after a concurrent receipt set the batch's expiry first)

index.description: The line's index in the request's lines array

reason.description: no-line-reference: the line named no document line; line-sku-mismatch: its SKU is not the referenced line's

code.description: Server-assigned code (GRN-<n>, unique per tenant)

poId.description: The PO booked against. Story 21-9: a receipt against a closed PO with an open carried successor is booked against the successor, named here

poCode.description: Story 21-9 — the successor PO's code; present only on a receipt re-targeted from a closed PO to its open successor

asnId.description: Story 21-6 — the ASN received against; present only on an ASN receipt

asnCode.description: Story 21-6 — the ASN's code; present only on an ASN receipt

clientId.description: Story 1-1 — the client whose goods the receipt booked (the PO's or ASN's client, or a blind receipt's chosen or derived client). Absent on a receipt replayed from before 1-1

gateInId.description: Story 2-3a — the gate-in the receipt is linked to; present only when linked

gateInCode.description: Story 2-3a — the linked gate-in's code; present only when linked

gateInLink.description: Story 2-3a — present only when the receipt named a gate-in that did NOT link (it booked unlinked)

status.description: recorded (the v1 terminal state)

occurredAt.description: Device time (AD-1), ISO-8601 UTC

unmatchedLines.description: Story 21-6 — present only when some lines of a PO/ASN receipt settled unmatched (booked in full, crediting no document line)

reviewOpId.description: Story 1-1 — the op id of the review row raised for the refused lines (Conflicts & Reviews, type `grn.lines-refused`, Discard only) — since 1-2a/1-2b every per-line refusal but `shelf-life-short` (which has its own row, `shelfLifeReviewOpId`); present only when one was raised

shelfLifeReviewOpId.description: Story 1-2b — the op id of the review row raised for the `shelf-life-short` lines (type `grn.shelf-life-refused` — Accept anyway with a note, or Discard); present only when one was raised

licenceReviewOpId.description: Story 1-6d — the op id of the review row raised for the `licence-not-covered` lines (type `grn.licence-refused` — an owner may accept them anyway with a note, or discard them); present only when one was raised

inactiveSkuReviewOpId.description: Story 1-4b — the op id of the review row raised for the blind or unmatched lines of an INACTIVE SKU this receipt booked (type `grn.inactive-sku-received` — Discard only, labelled Acknowledge; it books nothing); present only when one was raised

qcHeldLines.description: Story 1-2b — how many booked lines were put on receipt QC holds (the client's QC on receipt); present only when > 0

qcSkippedLines.description: Story 1-2b — how many booked lines of a QC-on-receipt client were NOT held because the SKU is serial-tracked or catch-weight; present only when > 0

recalledLots.description: Story 3-7a — the booked lots that sit on an open live recall: the receipt is booked and the lot stays blocked — keep the units apart. Present only when there is one

clientId.description: The client the blind receipt named — or (story 1-2a), when no client was named, the first refused line's client (a departed one)

occurredAt.description: Device time of the receipt (ISO-8601 UTC)

rejectedLines.description: Every request line, each `sku-client-mismatch` or (story 1-2a) `client-departed` or (story 1-2b) one of the expiry codes (`expiry-on-untracked`, `expiry-before-mfg`, `batch-expiry-mismatch`, `expiry-required`, `shelf-life-short`) or (story 1-6d) `licence-not-covered`

reviewOpId.description: The op id of the review row (`grn.lines-refused`, Discard only). Story 1-2b: absent when every line was refused `shelf-life-short` (only that row was raised)

shelfLifeReviewOpId.description: Story 1-2b — the op id of the `grn.shelf-life-refused` review row, when one was raised

licenceReviewOpId.description: Story 1-6d — the op id of the `grn.licence-refused` review row, when one was raised

gateInLink.description: Story 2-3a — present only when the receipt named a gate-in that did not link (nothing was recorded, so nothing linked)

goodsReceipt.description: The recorded GRN. Story 1-1 (decision 6): null when every line of a blind receipt was refused `sku-client-mismatch` — or (story 1-2a) every line of any receipt was refused `sku-client-mismatch` / `client-departed` — no receipt was recorded (no GRN code consumed); `refusedReceipt` then says what went to review

refusedReceipt.description: Story 1-1 — present only when goodsReceipt is null

uom.description: The level this barcode names — the SKU's base uom, or one of its pack levels

factor.description: Base units one scan of this barcode counts: the pack level's factor, or 1 at the base uom. The handheld adds it on receive, returns and pack; pick and putaway accept the barcode as SKU confirmation only.

unNumber.description: The UN number, four digits without the "UN" prefix

subsidiaryClasses.description: Up to two subsidiary DG classes, sorted

packingGroup.description: The UN packing group, or null

uomPrecision.description: Decimal places this SKU's base UoM may express (each = 0, kg = 3). The device validates entry against it OFFLINE, inside the Rejected banner, so a too-precise scan is refused before it is ever queued.

serialFormat.description: Story 2-6a: the serial format (`free` | `imei`) — the device's offline serial gate. A device whose snapshot lacks it (a pre-2-6a server) refuses to receive a serial-tracked SKU rather than capture anonymously

catchWeightTracked.description: Story 10.3: the SKU is handled by unit and priced by weight. It rides the snapshot so the device can PROMPT for a per-unit weight at receipt while offline — a prompt only the server knows about never happens on the floor.

variantValues.description: Story 11.7: this SKU's values on its product's declared variant axes, null when the SKU is unattached. Rides the snapshot so the device can SAY which variant a pick scan holds, offline (UX-DR28).

axes.description: Story 11.7: the attached product's declared variant axes, in declaration order — the order a variant label is read in. Null when the SKU is unattached.

storageClass.description: Story 12.8 (UX-DR29): the SKU's storage class (defaults to `ambient`). It rides the snapshot beside the bin arm's class so the device's offline conformance mirror can refuse a non-conforming placement or draw in the Rejected banner — a refusal only the server knew about would queue in a dead zone and come back hours later as a rejection the operator can no longer act on.

shelfLifeDays.description: Story 2-4b: the SKU's total shelf life in days from manufacture, or null. A receipt line of a batch-tracked SKU with a mfg date and no typed expiry gets expiry = mfg + this (server-side); the handheld previews it. Absent (an older server) or null = no preview

clientId.description: Story 1-1: the client the SKU belongs to. Code and barcode are unique per (tenant, client), so one barcode may name several SKUs; the device resolves a scan through the work's own SKUs first, then the document's client (`clients` names each)

packBarcodes.description: Story 1-4: every non-primary barcode of the SKU with its level and factor (1 at the base uom). Empty when the SKU has none; an older device ignores it.

status.description: Story 1-4b: `inactive` — the SKU takes no new inbound. A receive scan of it that is not on the document is still booked and flagged for review; the handheld warns at scan time. An older device ignores it.

fragile.description: Story 1-6a: handle with care — the handheld notes it on receive, pick, pack and putaway

highValue.description: Story 1-6a: a handling and insurance marker — noted on the handheld, never a placement rule

maxStackLayers.description: Story 1-6a: how many of the SKU's outermost received units may stand on one another (1 = do not stack); shown, not enforced

dg.description: Story 1-6a: the dangerous-goods identity, null when the SKU is not a dangerous good

isKit.description: Story 3-1: the SKU is a kit (a kit holds no stock — the handheld refuses a move of it offline). An older server omits it; the device reads absence as false

clientId.description: Story 1-1 (additive): the PO's client — the device resolves an unmatched scan within it

vendorName.description: Story 1-3 — the vendor's name as the PO froze it (the handheld's receive card shows it; an older server omits it)

lines.description: Per-line ordered / received / open quantities

announcedQty.description: Announced quantity. A quantity in the SKU's base UoM, at the decimal precision that unit declares (each = 0 places, kg = 3). A value finer than its unit allows is refused, naming the unit and its precision — never silently rounded.

receivedQty.description: Received to date, in base UoM

openQty.description: Derived: announcedQty − receivedQty, clamped at 0 for display (story 1-2b — received may pass announced after an approved over-receipt or a within-tolerance receipt)

code.description: The client-supplied ASN code

expectedAt.description: When the shipment is expected (ISO-8601 UTC), null when unannounced

type.description: The fixed location type (12-4 vocabulary): shelf, pallet, floor, staging, floor-stack, yard, tank or silo

blocked.description: Broken-bin flag — blocked bins reject placements

blockedReason.description: Story 3-3b — why the bin is blocked (null while active); the handheld names it on its refusals. A client reading a snapshot cached before 3-3b treats an absent field as null

systemOwned.description: System bins (Receiving/QC-hold) are never placement targets

frozen.description: Story 3-5b — the bin is frozen for a stock take: the handheld refuses every movement into or out of it offline (count it, or wait for the take to close). A client reading a snapshot cached before 3-5b treats an absent field as false

storageClass.description: Story 12.8 (UX-DR29): the bin's storage class (defaults to `ambient`). It rides the snapshot beside the SKU arm's class (the catalog snapshot) so the device's offline conformance mirror can refuse a non-conforming placement in the Rejected banner — before anything queues.

dedicatedClientId.description: Story 1-5b: the client this bin is dedicated to (null = shared). A dedicated bin refuses any other client's stock; the device mirrors the rule offline (the snapshot `clients` arm names the client), the server re-gates at placement and transfer receive.

code.description: The LPN code — what the pallet or carton label's barcode encodes, byte for byte

qty.description: The declared quantity on the label, base units
min(applied, receiving-bin on-hand) — the placeable units

suggestedBin.description: The suggested bin; null when no storage bin has room

serialNumbers.description: Story 2-6a — present only on a SERIAL-TRACKED task: the GRN line's booked serial numbers still in the Receiving bin, in capture order (qty is their count). The handheld verifies each scan against this list offline; a serial task without it (an older server, a legacy anonymous line) cannot be placed from the handheld

lpns.description: Story 2-10b — the GRN line's ACTIVE LPNs (licence plates) in code order; empty when none. A handheld scan of one chooses this task, verified, with the quantity prefilled (min of the LPN's and the task's). Placed and voided LPNs never appear

kitParentSkuCode.description: Story 11.7: the parent kit SKU's code when this task's order line is a kit component (order_lines.parent_line_id), null on an ordinary line. Display-only — the device renders "from kit {code}" in the task header; no pick logic reads kit-ness.

orderPriority.description: Story 4-2a — the task's order priority (display: the stop's chip). The walk stays in bin order.

skuId.description: The SKU the unit belongs to

orderReference.description: The order's channel reference; null for a manual order

clientId.description: Story 1-1 (additive): the order's client — the device resolves a typed code within it after the RMA's own lines

batchCode.description: The batch the pick must scan (null on an untracked SKU)

qty.description: Units to pick (base units) — the pick takes at most this

rmaCode.description: The RMA the returned units came back on (returns lines)

receivingToleranceBps.description: Over-receipt tolerance, basis points of the ordered / announced quantity (500 = 5 %)

qcOnReceipt.description: Booked lines are put on receipt QC holds

expiryRequired.description: A batch-tracked line needs an expiry date

minShelfLifeDays.description: Minimum remaining shelf life in IST calendar days, or null

deriveExpiry.description: Story 2-4b — the server sets a batch's expiry from mfg + the SKU's shelfLifeDays when no expiry is typed (the device previews it). Absent (an older server) reads as true

code.description: The client code (the tenant's own client's is `self`)

name.description: The display name (the tenant's own client carries the tenant's name)

active.description: False when suspended or departed — a blind receipt picks only an active client

unloadStartedAt.description: ISO-8601 UTC, null until the unload started

appointment.description: Story 2-3b (additive) — the linked dock appointment, read-only; null = unscheduled. An older server omits it

noteRequired.description: The reason needs a note beside it (the reason `other`)

label.description: The operator-facing label (the web uses the same words)

parcelTagCode.description: The parcel tag code (`O` + the order id’s last 16 hex digits)

packSeq.description: Story 4-5a (D6, additive): the live pack’s number — a carton label of a lower pack is stale. Absent for an order packed before cartons were recorded (pack 1, one carton) and from an older server

cartonCount.description: Story 4-5a (D6, additive): the live pack’s carton count; absent as packSeq

codAmountPaise.description: Story 4-5a (A44, additive): the COD amount in paise (carton 1 carries the COD label); absent when prepaid

openPurchaseOrders.description: The warehouse's open POs with their lines

openAsns.description: Story 21-6 (additive): the warehouse's open advance shipment notices (announced or partially received) with per-line announced / received / open — receiving books against them exactly as against a PO

bins.description: Story 3.5 (additive): every bin of the warehouse — blocked/system bins included so the device can reject a scan against them pre-queue

putawayTasks.description: Story 3.5 (additive): the derived putaway tasks with the capacity-only suggestions (advisory — the server re-gates at placement)

pickTasks.description: Story 4.3 (additive): the pick tasks of every ready picklist on a released wave — story 4-2a: whole picklists by urgency (the most urgent planned order of each picklist, judged on the snapshot IST date), each in walk order (the bin/batch each names is advisory — the server re-derives both at pick time)

packTasks.description: Story 10.7 (additive): the packable orders' per-SKU picked totals — the dataset the bench pre-verifies its scan against, offline. Mirrors the pack command's own verification query (picks grouped by (order, sku)) and its completeness guards (accepted, ≥1 pick line, none planned, not all cancelled)

handlingUnits.description: Story 10.7 (additive): every ACTIVE handling unit of the warehouse (id + skuId) — the labels a catch-weight bench scan resolves against, offline. Active-only self-prunes (units flip to packed at pack)

transferTasks.description: Story 5-1 (additive): the in-transit transfers TO this warehouse — the Transfer inbox tasks whose inbound confirm the operator executes (one confirm completes the whole order)

countTasks.description: Story 5-3 (additive): the STORED pending count tasks of this warehouse — the Count inbox tasks whose submit the operator executes (every task line must be counted; 0 is a valid explicit count). The expectations were FROZEN at task start and are read here, never recomputed

stockTakes.description: Story 3-5b (additive): the warehouse's counting (and posting) stock takes — the handheld groups their count tasks by zone and refuses movements into or out of a frozen bin (bins[].frozen). An older server omits it

openReturns.description: Story 13-2 (additive): the warehouse's return authorizations that can still receive (open or partially received) — the handheld receives returned units against them offline, grading each unit; units not on an authorization are queued for review, never refused on the device

openVendorReturns.description: Story 2-8b (additive): the warehouse's DRAFT returns to vendor, oldest first — the handheld's Returns out tab picks them scan-verified (rtv.pick). An older server omits it

openClientReturns.description: Story 4-7c (additive): the warehouse's DRAFT returns to client, oldest first — the handheld's Returns out tab picks them scan-verified (rtc.pick) beside the returns to vendor. An older server omits it

clients.description: Story 1-1 (additive): every client referenced by a SKU or an open document of the snapshot — the names the device shows when a scan belongs to another client, and the blind receipt's client picker. A snapshot WITHOUT this field (an older server) puts the device in legacy mode: no picker, no clientId sent

openGateIns.description: Story 2-3a (additive): the warehouse's open gate-ins — not gated out, gated in within the last 7 days, at most 200, newest first (decision 15). The dock records their unload and receives against them. An older server omits it

dockAppointments.description: Story 2-3b (additive): the warehouse's BOOKED dock appointments starting today (IST, server clock), at most 100, by start — the Receive tab's read-only "Expected today". The device derives "Not arrived" from endsAt + graceMinutes against its own clock. An older server omits it

receiptDamageReasons.description: Story 2-4a (additive): the damage reason vocabulary — the handheld shows its Damaged control only when the snapshot carries it (an older server omits it), and refuses to confirm a draft holding damage against a snapshot without it

receiptShortReasons.description: Story 2-4a (additive): the short reason vocabulary — the Short control's gate, as receiptDamageReasons

receiptPhotos.description: Story 2-5a (additive): damage photos on a receipt line — whether storage is on (the Photo button's gate) and the caps the draft must respect. An older server omits it, and the handheld then offers no Photo

moveReasons.description: Story 3-1 (additive): the bin-to-bin move's reason vocabulary, in order — the handheld's reason chips. A reason with noteRequired needs a note (up to 200 characters). An older server omits it, and the handheld then offers no Move stock

adjustReasons.description: Story 3-2b (additive): the stock adjustment's reason vocabulary with labels, in order — the handheld's Adjust reason chips (every reason needs the note the adjustment always carries). An older server omits it, and the handheld then offers no Adjust

dispatchParcels.description: Story 4-4a (additive): the parcels awaiting a courier — the warehouse's packed orders, plus its accepted orders holding a live client-arranged shipment (never one with a carrier shipment), at most 2000, oldest first. The pack bench verifies a client label against it; the handover matches scanned AWBs and parcel tags against it. An older server omits it (the device reads it as empty)

dispatchParcelsTruncated.description: Story 4-4a (additive): true when dispatchParcels was capped at 2000 — hand over newer parcels on the web, or refresh later

packCartons.description: Story 4-5a (A32, additive): true when this server records cartons on a pack — the handheld offers New carton only then. Absent from an older server (which would drop `cartons` from a synced pack): one carton only

blindReasonCode.description: Set only on a blind receipt
